original_title: Hydrogel-based delivery of extracellular vesicles for skin wound healing: design strategies, therapeutic mechanisms, and translational perspectives.
title: A hydrogel to keep extracellular vesicles where the wound actually is
blurb: A review of hydrogel carriers for delivering extracellular vesicles to skin wounds, covering how they're designed, what they're supposed to be doing therapeutically, and how close any of it is to actual translation.

original_title: Electronic and Steric Effects on the Photoswitching and Thermal Relaxation of Ortho ‐Substituted Pyrazole Azo Phthalimides
title: One CF3 group moves your photoswitch from UV to green light
blurb: Four ortho-substituted phthalimide-azopyrazole switches (CH3, CF3, tert-Bu, Ph) show that swapping in CF3 alone pushes E to Z photoisomerization out to 530 nm, while the rest still need 370 nm. The attainable Z-rich states barely budge across the set, so what you're buying is wavelength control, not better switching.

original_title: Acetate-Enabled Selective Electrochemical Deuterolysis of Propargylic Carbonates
title: D2O as your deuterium source, no exotic reagents required
blurb: A nickel-electrocatalyzed platform converts propargylic carbonates into deuterated allenes using plain D2O as the deuterium source, with acetate steering the selectivity. It covers 1,3-dialkyl allenes, the kind that actually turn up in nature, with excellent isotopic incorporation, useful given how fiddly selective deuteration usually is.

original_title: Novel Gram-negative bacteria hydrogel radiation dosimeters: Water equivalence and comparison with Gram-positive bacterial dosimeter
title: Bacteria as radiation dosimeters, now with a Gram-negative option
blurb: A hydrogel dosimeter built around Gram-negative bacteria, checked for water equivalence and compared against an existing Gram-positive version. Niche, but dosimetry is always hunting for cheap water-equivalent standins, and bacteria are cheaper than most.

original_title: Subnanometer Ni@Fe Catalysts Enable High-Performance and Stable Oxygen Evolution of WO3 Photoanodes
title: Subnanometer Ni@Fe coating pushes WO3 photoanodes to a record photocurrent
blurb: Trimesic acid pins subnanometer Ni@Fe hydroxide clusters onto nanoporous WO3, and the resulting photoanode hits a record ~2.4 mA/cm² at 1.23 V RHE under full sun, with notably better stability than bare WO3. The precise subnanometer placement is the actual trick, not just piling on more NiFe.

original_title: Electrochemically Driven Phenazine Autoxidation Coupled With Supported Liquid Membrane Technology for Hydrogen Peroxide Production
title: Keeping H2O2 production and decomposition from undoing each other
blurb: Direct electrosynthesis of H2O2 usually self-destructs because the product forms and decomposes right at the same electrode interface. This pairs electrochemically driven phenazine autoxidation with a supported liquid membrane to physically separate the two steps, aimed at making electrified H2O2 production scalable rather than just a neat lab cell.

original_title: Flexible‐Ligand Rigidification Enables Anti‐Thermal‐Quenching Emission and Cryogenic Afterglow in Antimony‐Based Hybrid Bimetallic Halides
title: Freezing a floppy ligand to stop luminescence from dying when it's hot
blurb: Flexible urea ligands are usually why hybrid halide emitters fade at higher temperature. Rigidify them inside zero-dimensional antimony-based bimetallic chlorides like [RE(DEU)6]SbCl6 and the self-trapped-exciton emission resists thermal quenching, with cryogenic afterglow as a bonus across a whole family of rare-earth variants.

original_title: Beyond Push–Pull Chromophores: Unlocking the Synthetic Potential of Formal [2+2] CA‐RE for Quinolone Annulation
title: An old push-pull dye reaction repurposed to build quinolines metal-free
blurb: The CA-RE cycloaddition-retroelectrocyclization reaction normally just makes push-pull chromophores. Here they intercept its intermediate with an intramolecular nucleophilic cyclization instead, turning o-aminophenyl alkynes and dicyanoalkenes into dicyanovinyl dihydroquinolines without a metal catalyst in sight.

original_title: Rh(III)-Catalyzed Annulation of Enaminones with Sulfoxonium Ylides: Access to Isoquinolines and Benzo[ de ]chromenes
title: Rh(III) annulation finds a different reason for its site selectivity
blurb: Enaminones plus sulfoxonium ylides give isoquinolines under Cp*Rh catalysis with AgOAc and PivOH, moderate to excellent yields, nothing shocking there. The interesting bit is the proposed mechanism: site selectivity looks driven by Lewis acid-enaminone interactions rather than the usual carbonyl-directed C-H activation.

original_title: PSMA Biology Through the Clinical Lens: Implications for Radioligand Therapy of Prostate Cancer with [(177)Lu]Lu-PSMA-617.
title: What PSMA biology actually buys you with Lu-177-PSMA-617
blurb: A clinical review tying PSMA biology back to how [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 performs as radioligand therapy in prostate cancer. No new data, just the framework connecting the receptor science to what shows up in patients.

original_title: Reprogramming Stereocontrol Through Progressive Substrate Reorganization in Artificial Triplet Photoenzymes
title: Tuning an artificial photoenzyme by reorganizing the substrate, not the photosensitizer
blurb: Artificial triplet photoenzymes usually have no real link between where the photosensitizer sits and how the substrate is held, which makes stereocontrol a crapshoot. Crystallography, kinetics, simulation, and protein engineering trace the enantioselectivity of TPe4.0_FBpA's [2+2] cycloaddition to how tightly its cavity organizes the indole substrate, and remodeling that pocket step by step is what actually dials in the selectivity.

original_title: Mechanistic Characterization of a Multiproduct Sesquiterpene Synthase for Triquinanes and Quadranes from Streptomyces pathocidini
title: One terpene synthase, a whole pile of triquinanes and quadranes
blurb: Genome mining turned up a sesquiterpene synthase from Streptomyces pathocidini that refuses to commit to a single product. Isotope labeling and DFT work out the branching cyclization mechanism, and site-directed mutagenesis pulls out four more products, one of which the wild-type enzyme was already making in trace amounts.

original_title: Unraveling the Importance of Surface Hydrogen Diffusion in Photocatalysis by Isotope Probing
title: Hydrogen evolution's hidden bottleneck might just be diffusion
blurb: Using a well-defined Pt/TiO2(110) photocatalyst, time-resolved mass spec, and methanol isotopologues to trace where each hydrogen atom actually comes from, they find surface hydrogen diffusion is a real, previously overlooked limit on photocatalytic hydrogen evolution, not just the usual suspects.

original_title: Framework Deuteration Regulates Excited-State Dynamics and H2O2 Release in Covalent Organic Framework Photocatalysis
title: Swapping H for D in a COF boosts its H2O2 output by 80%
blurb: Same framework, same crystallinity, porosity, and ground-state electronics, just deuterated. D-TpPa makes H2O2 1.8x faster than H-TpPa in pure water under O2, and the spectroscopy points to weaker exciton-phonon coupling as the reason, a clean isotope effect with nothing else to blame it on.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Using All Probes Plasmids to Lower the Barrier for Quantifying Single-mRNA Translation Dynamics in Live Cells.
title: A plasmid kit for watching single mRNAs get translated live
blurb: A methods paper on "all probes" plasmids meant to make imaging single-mRNA translation dynamics in live cells easier to set up, lowering the barrier to entry rather than changing what's measured.

original_title: Subtype-Specific Enrichment of HER2-Positive Extracellular Vesicles Enables Metabolomic Profiling for Breast Cancer Liquid Biopsy
title: Fishing HER2-positive exosomes out of blood for a metabolomics liquid biopsy
blurb: Liquid biopsy EV work usually nets a mixed bag of vesicles that muddies the mass spec. Phage display turned up HER2-targeting peptides, built into a magnetic bead platform (SA@HER2-2-MPMs) that selectively pulls out HER2-positive extracellular vesicles, clean enough as a subpopulation to actually run LC-MS/MS metabolomics on for breast cancer.

original_title: Process Development of ABBV-576: A C2 Corrector for the Treatment of Cystic Fibrosis
title: A second-generation route for ABBV-576, oxidation step included
blurb: Process chemists rebuilding the manufacturing route for this CFTR C2 corrector after the first phase I batch exposed its weak points. The new sequence runs a branch-selective Mizoroki-Heck, a Sharpless asymmetric dihydroxylation/cyclization, then an alcohol-to-acid oxidation on a substrate that would rather fall apart than oxidize, capped with the amide coupling that forges the actual drug. This is the unglamorous part of drug development that decides whether phase I happens at all.

original_title: Tau positron emission tomography harmonization using the CenTauR approach: General conversion equations, relevant cut-points, and external validation.
title: A conversion scale so tau PET scans from different trackers actually agree
blurb: The CenTauR approach gives tau PET its own harmonization scheme, with conversion equations and cutpoints checked against an external dataset so results from different tracers and pipelines can be compared on one scale, the way Centiloid did for amyloid.

original_title: Sc(OTf)3-Catalyzed Reaction of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes with Isatins toward Cyclobutene–Indolinone Scaffolds Bearing Contiguous Stereocenters
title: Bicyclobutanes meet isatins and come out with two new stereocenters
blurb: Sc(OTf)3 opens up 1,3-disubstituted bicyclobutanes and adds them across isatins, building cyclobutene-indolinone scaffolds with two contiguous chiral centers under mild conditions. Yields run up to 84% with broad substrate tolerance, but the diastereoselectivity only hits 12:1 at best, so some of these batches won't separate cleanly.

original_title: Anion-Exchange Strategy for the Optimization of Cu2MnS2-xSe x Nanostructures toward Bifunctional Electrocatalysis in Alkaline Water Splitting
title: Swapping sulfur for selenium to tune a water-splitting catalyst
blurb: A hydrothermal anion-exchange series across Cu2MnS2-xSex, dialing selenium content from zero to full swap. More selenium distorts the lattice and shifts the electronics of the Cu-Mn framework, which the authors tie to better charge transport and more accessible active sites for both halves of alkaline water splitting.

original_title: Photochemical Generation and Spectroscopic Characterization of Parent 3‐Iminooxetane and 3‐Oxazoline From 3‐Azidooxetane
title: Freezing argon at 3 K to catch two oxetane imines nobody had pinned down
blurb: UV photolysis of 3-azidooxetane trapped in argon at 3 K burns off the azide and leaves two C3H5NO isomers, 3-iminooxetane and 3-oxazoline, identified by IR against anharmonic calculations and confirmed with deuterium labeling. Simple heterocyclic imines like these matter for prebiotic and astrochemical questions, and apparently the parent compounds had never actually been characterized before.

original_title: Electronic Modulation-Driven Dual Self-Reconstruction of a Nickel–Molybdenum Oxide Catalyst for Durable and Highly Efficient Anion-Exchange-Membrane Water Electrolysis
title: A nickel-molybdenum catalyst that rebuilds itself into two different jobs
blurb: Doping a nickel-molybdenum oxide precatalyst with iron and vanadium steers how it reconstructs in situ, so it settles into one stable active phase under hydrogen evolution conditions and a different one under oxygen evolution. The point is a single precatalyst that's durable and efficient on both electrodes of an anion-exchange-membrane electrolyzer, instead of needing two separate catalysts.

original_title: Inverse-IMPRESSION: A Graph-Based Platform for Molecular Structure Elucidation from Experimental NMR Spectroscopic Properties
title: Running NMR spectra backward to get the molecule out
blurb: Inverse-IMPRESSION takes experimental NMR parameters straight to a bonding network with a graph transformer, then cleans up the guess by stripping out shaky bonds and reassigning them, then runs a noise-augmented ensemble to generate candidate structures. Structure elucidation as a model you feed spectra into rather than a puzzle you solve by hand.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Applying plasma as an etching technique for CN-85 SSNTDs: Comparison study
title: Plasma etching put up against the usual method on CN-85 track detectors
blurb: A comparison study testing plasma etching as an alternative to chemical etching on CN-85 solid-state nuclear track detectors.

original_title: What Determines the Charge State Distribution of Proteins Electrosprayed from Non-Denaturing Solutions?
title: Protein ions keep shedding charge even after they've dried out
blurb: Electrospraying BSA or ovalbumin from ammonium acetate or triethylammonium formate into dry air and isolating a single charge state in under a millisecond shows the protein ion keeps losing charge by ion evaporation even once the solvent is gone and it's sitting there dry. That's a problem for the usual story that max charge is set by droplet size via Rayleigh's limit or small-ion evaporation while the solvent is still around.

original_title: A Study to Compare DB-1303/BNT323 Versus T-DM1 in Breast Cancer
title: DualityBio's HER2 ADC goes head to head with T-DM1
blurb: Phase 3, active but not recruiting: DB-1303/BNT323 tested against T-DM1, the established HER2 antibody-drug conjugate, in HER2-positive breast cancer. Sponsor is DualityBio, and beating T-DM1 head-to-head rather than just adding another option is the actual bar here.

original_title: First-in-human trial shows B7-H4 antibody-drug conjugate shrinks ovarian, endometrial and breast tumors - Bioengineer.org
title: A B7-H4 antibody-drug conjugate shrinks tumors in its first human trial
blurb: First-in-human results for a B7-H4-targeted ADC report shrinkage across ovarian, endometrial and breast tumors. B7-H4 barely shows up on normal tissue, which is the whole selling point of the target, so it's a promising early read, but it's one trial's headline, not the dataset.

original_title: B7-H4‒directed antibody-drug conjugate AZD8205 (puxitatug samrotecan) in patients with advanced/metastatic solid tumors: the Phase 1/2a (BLUESTAR), first-in-human study
title: AZD8205 hits B7-H4 tumors with a bystander payload
blurb: First-in-human Phase 1/2a (BLUESTAR) data on AZD8205, aka puxitatug samrotecan: a B7-H4-directed ADC with a stable cleavable linker and a topoisomerase-1 payload that can also kill neighboring, antigen-negative cells. 47 patients with B7-H4-positive endometrial, ovarian or breast cancer, or cholangiocarcinoma, got dosed. B7-H4 is attractive precisely because normal tissue barely expresses it while progressing tumors ramp it up, so there's an actual target here if the responses hold up.

original_title: Controlling Radical Reactivity for Visible‐Light Bioorthogonal Chemistry
title: Dialing in which radicals survive long enough to be bioorthogonal
blurb: Visible-light photocatalysis makes carbon-centered radicals cheaply via single-electron transfer, but that doesn't mean they stay well-behaved around a cell's native chemistry. This is the first systematic look at controlling that radical reactivity itself, so the coupling hits the intended exogenous partner instead of whatever biological group happens to be nearby.

original_title: Single-domain antibody-conjugated lipid nanoparticles for selective mRNA delivery to CD4⁺ T cells and Brec1-mediated excision of HIV-1 proviral DNA
title: Targeting CD4 T cells with mRNA to cut HIV out of hiding
blurb: Lipid nanoparticles tagged with a CD4-specific nanobody deliver mRNA encoding Brec1, a designer recombinase that excises integrated HIV-1 proviral DNA, directly into the T cells that harbor the latent reservoir. Proof-of-concept only, but targeted delivery into resting reservoir cells has been the actual bottleneck for this kind of cure for years, not the excision enzyme itself.

original_title: Lonza expands Visp bioconjugation manufacturing capacity to complete 2028 - Cleanroom Technology
title: Lonza bets on more bioconjugation capacity at Visp through 2028
blurb: Lonza is expanding bioconjugation manufacturing capacity at its Visp site, targeting completion by 2028. Reads as a bet that ADC demand keeps outrunning supply rather than news about any specific molecule.

original_title: Multivalent antiviral conjugates enhance activity against Influenza via cross-linking viruses.
title: Cross-linking flu virions instead of just blocking them
blurb: Multivalent conjugates boost antiviral activity against influenza by cross-linking virus particles together rather than targeting one at a time. Published in Nat Commun, but the snippet is thin, so this is mechanism, not numbers yet.

original_title: Dual‑payload antibody‑drug conjugates in triple‑negative breast cancer: Preclinical advances and future perspectives (Review)
title: Two payloads, one antibody, still fighting TNBC's heterogeneity problem
blurb: A review of dual-payload ADCs for triple-negative breast cancer, the pitch being that two different warheads on one antibody counter the tumor heterogeneity that lets single-payload ADCs lose efficacy over time. Preclinical only, and the review itself flags heterogeneity as the thing still limiting these constructs.

original_title: Orthogonal Chemical Encoding Enables Sequence‐Independent GlycoRNA Imaging in Organoids and Tissues
title: Imaging glycoRNA without needing to know its sequence
blurb: COMPASS tags terminal sialic acids with azides and nascent uridines with alkynes, then reads out proximity between the two to visualize glycosylated RNA without sequence-specific probes or bulky DNA nanostructures. That sequence independence is what finally lets it work in organoids and tissue, not just the simplified cultured cells every earlier glycoRNA imaging method was stuck with.

original_title: Optimization of [<sup>18</sup>F]Fallypride synthesis for distribution over long distances
title: Making F-18 fallypride survive the trip to the scanner
blurb: An optimization of [18F]Fallypride synthesis aimed at shipping it over long distances, basically squeezing more usable tracer out of a batch before fluorine-18's short half-life eats the dose. Logistics paper more than chemistry.

original_title: ESMO: Bristol Myers CMO touts ‘5 out of 5’ positive phase 3 trials for bispecific ADC iza-bren - Fierce Pharma
title: BMS claims a perfect five-for-five for its bispecific ADC
blurb: At ESMO, Bristol Myers' CMO touted iza-bren going 5 for 5 across its Phase 3 trials. That's the company's own framing from a conference podium, not a publication, so treat the scorecard as a pitch until the actual readouts are in print.

original_title: Interplays Between Therapeutic Radiopharmaceuticals and Tumor Microenvironment.
title: The tumor microenvironment talks back to radiopharmaceuticals
blurb: A review of how therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals and the tumor microenvironment interact, hypoxia, immune cells, and stroma all shaping how well a radiation dose actually lands, and the dose shaping them right back.

original_title: Applications of TMSN 3 in Photo‐ and Electrocatalytic Organic Synthesis
title: TMSN3 as the cheap azide everyone's reaching for
blurb: A mini-review rounding up where trimethylsilyl azide has muscled into photocatalytic and electrocatalytic synthesis as an azide/amine source, plus the mechanisms behind it. Cheap and easy to get is probably the whole reason it's spreading, but this is a survey piece, not a new reaction.

original_title: Heptacyclic Skeleton Construction in the Total Synthesis of Hetisine‐Type C 20 ‐Diterpenoid Alkaloids
title: Building the seven-ring cage of hetisine alkaloids
blurb: A minireview walking through every total synthesis so far of hetisine-type C20-diterpenoid alkaloids, that 6/6/6/6/5/5/5 heptacyclic frame with nine contiguous stereocenters, three all-carbon quaternary centers, and a N–C6 bridge that's wrecked plenty of synthetic plans. It's a tour of which strategic tricks actually worked, not a new route.

original_title: Frontispiece: Regioselective Hydroarylation of Internal and Terminal Alkenes With N ‐Aryl Pyrazoles Enabled by Lanthanum Catalysts
title: Lanthanum catalysts arylate alkenes on either end
blurb: Regioselective hydroarylation of both internal and terminal alkenes with N-aryl pyrazoles, run through lanthanum catalysis. The regiocontrol across two different alkene classes with the same metal is the part worth noting.

original_title: Triple-signal-amplified competitive immunoassay based on bifunctional multivalent nanobody for high-sensitivity detection of ochratoxin a in coffee.
title: A nanobody pulling triple duty to catch ochratoxin A in your coffee
blurb: A competitive immunoassay built on a bifunctional multivalent nanobody that stacks three signal-amplification tricks to push up sensitivity for detecting ochratoxin A in coffee. The multivalent, triple-amplified nanobody is the actual gimmick here, not just another ELISA swap.

original_title: ANALYTICAL METHOD DEVELOPMENT AND FORCE DEGRADATION STUDIES OF ANALYTICAL QUALITY BY DESIGN (AQBD) BASED OPTIMIZATION OFA RP-UPLC METHOD FOR DETERMINATION OF NIVOLUMAB INJECTION
title: Nivolumab gets the Quality-by-Design treatment for its stability assay
blurb: A stability-indicating RP-UPLC method for nivolumab injections, tuned via Analytical Quality by Design with a five-level, three-factor central composite design in Design-Expert, then stress-tested with forced degradation studies. Solid, unglamorous QC chemistry, the kind every biologic needs and rarely gets written up this carefully.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

original_title: Trifunctional zirconium catalysis-enabled triple modular synthesis
title: Zirconium catalysis stops just sitting there as a Lewis acid
blurb: Zirconium's mostly been stuck doing Lewis acid and redox chemistry with the occasional photocatalytic C–H activation. This trifunctional version wires photochemical, redox, and Lewis acid reactivity into one cycle to build benzylamines straight from alkanes, aldehydes, and nitriles, modular synthesis from three reactivity modes at once is the actual news.

original_title: ANALYTICAL METHOD DEVELOPMENT AND FORCE DEGRADATION STUDIES OF ANALYTICAL QUALITY BY DESIGN (AQBD) BASED OPTIMIZATION OFA RP-UPLC METHOD FOR DETERMINATION OF NIVOLUMAB INJECTION
title: Nivolumab gets the Quality-by-Design treatment for its stability assay
blurb: A stability-indicating RP-UPLC method for nivolumab injections, tuned via Analytical Quality by Design with a five-level, three-factor central composite design in Design-Expert, then stress-tested with forced degradation studies. Solid, unglamorous QC chemistry, the kind every biologic needs and rarely gets written up this carefully.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

original_title: Molybdenum-Catalyzed Reductive C–N Coupling/Cyclization Cascade for the De Novo Construction of N -Substituted Oxindoles
title: A molybdenum cascade builds oxindoles from scratch
blurb: A Mo-catalyzed reductive C–N coupling/cyclization cascade that builds N-substituted oxindoles de novo from cheap starting materials, with broad functional group tolerance and late enough stage reach to touch biorelevant targets. Practical over flashy, which seems to be the point.

original_title: Stereodivergent Synthesis of γ-Functionalized Primary Alcohols via Relay-Synergistic Ir/Amine/Ni Catalysis
title: Finally functionalizing primary alcohols past the alpha and beta spots
blurb: Alpha and beta functionalization of primary alcohols is old news; gamma has been the holdout. A relay-synergistic Ir/amine/Ni system converts primary allylic alcohols into gamma-functionalized products with adjacent stereocenters, and does it stereodivergently so you pick the diastereomer. Three catalysts running in relay is a lot to keep synchronized, but it closes a real gap if it holds up outside the paper.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Recent progress and future perspectives in asymmetric aldol catalysis
title: Asymmetric aldol catalysis, the decades-later roundup
blurb: A review tour through proline-based organocatalysis from List and MacMillan, chiral Cu and Ni complexes, and heterogeneous recyclable catalysts, plus variants like vinylogous and nitroso aldols. No new chemistry here, just a map of where the field's many branches currently stand.
venue: Journal of King Saud University - Science

original_title: ANALYTICAL VALIDATION OF STABILITY-INDICATING METHOD FOR ESTIMATION OF ANTIHYPERTENSIVE DRUGS USING REVERSE PHASE ULTRA-PERFORMANCE LIQUID CHROMATOGRAPHY: A REVIEW
title: Yet another RP-UPLC method review for blood pressure drugs
blurb: A review of stability-indicating RP-UPLC methods for antihypertensive drugs, covering why fast, high-resolution, low-solvent chromatography is the default for checking identity, strength, and purity. Standard pharma-analytics ground, no new assay reported.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

original_title: A REVIEW ON METHOD DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF SELECTED ANTINEOPLASTIC DRUG TREOSULFAN BY USING DIFFERENT ANALYTICAL TECHNIQUES
title: Treosulfan finally gets its own method-review roundup
blurb: A review of analytical techniques for quantifying treosulfan, the pH-activated alkylating prodrug used to prep patients for stem-cell transplants. A survey of existing methods rather than a new one.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

original_title: Surfactant‐Assisted Cascade Synthesis of Tetrahydroquinoline Cyanocarboxamides Through Intramolecular Hydride‐Transfer Cyclization in Aqueous CTAB Media
title: CTAB water skips the usual hydride-transfer headaches
blurb: Ortho-aminobenzaldehydes and cyanoacetamide-type active methylene compounds cyclize in aqueous CTAB via intramolecular hydride transfer, giving tetrahydroquinoline cyanocarboxamides in good yield and diastereoselectivity. Works with glycine, malononitrile, ethyl cyanoacetate, and barbituric acid as the methylene partner, all in water with no exotic catalyst.

original_title: Multienzyme Cascade Reactions: Compatibility, Cooperativity, and Control
title: Running several enzymes in one pot without them tripping over each other
blurb: A review of multienzyme cascades from roughly the last five years, organized around the real headache of combining biocatalytic steps: whether the enzymes are compatible, whether they cooperate, and how you control the overall process. The payoff is skipping intermediate isolation and reaching transformations no single enzyme step could manage alone.

original_title: Demonstration of a Two‐Electron Pathway in Piezoelectric Mechanochemistry: Synthesis and Mechanical Adaptation of Polythiourethane
title: Ultrasound and vibration run two electron-transfer pathways in the same pot
blurb: Ball milling mechanochemistry usually picks either a radical or a two-electron pathway. This one uses focused ultrasound plus mechanical vibration to get both thiol reactions happening at once, building a polythiourethane, and which pathway wins depends on the reactive partner, which they use to bias the final product.

original_title: Alcohols as carbene precursors via formal 1,1-elimination
title: Turning alcohols into carbenes without the usual leaving-group setup
blurb: 1,2-elimination from an alcohol gives you an alkene, easy. This is the 1,1 version: formal C-H activation and alpha-elimination of the hydroxyl turn a plain monofunctional alcohol into a carbene equivalent, no preinstalled difunctionality required. A new route to carbene reactivity out of one of the cheapest feedstocks around.

original_title: A versatile and simple dual-network oxime hydrogel delivery system for fine-tuning of release kinetics.
title: An oxime hydrogel that lets you dial in release speed
blurb: A dual-network hydrogel built on oxime linkages, designed so release kinetics can be tuned just by adjusting the network rather than reformulating the whole system. Simple by design, which is the point.

original_title: KO t Bu‐Catalyzed Construction of Fully Substituted Phosphate Ester‐Functionalized 5‐Thioureido‐Triazoles
title: A thioureido-triazole three-for-one, no metal required
blurb: KOtBu alone drives a three-component coupling of nitriles, azides, and phosphoroisothiocyanatidates into fully substituted phosphate ester-functionalized 5-thioureido-triazoles. The nitrile-azide cycloaddition forms a triazole anion intermediate that then grabs the phosphoroisothiocyanatidate, all transition-metal-free with broad substrate scope and high regioselectivity.

original_title: Synthetic auxotrophy reveals metabolic regulation of plasma cell generation, affinity maturation, and cytokine receptor signaling
title: Starve B cells of glutamine and plasma cell output drops, but not for the reason you'd guess
blurb: Using synthetic auxotrophy to control nutrient supply, they find restricting glutamine cuts B cell proliferation and plasma cell differentiation, but glutaminolysis itself, the pathway everyone assumed was doing the work, turns out to be only conditionally necessary. Affinity maturation and cytokine receptor signaling trace back to the same metabolic regulation.

original_title: Ligand hardness as a key feature differentiating base- versus noble-metal mechanisms of nickel-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura cross-couplings
title: Why some nickel cross-couplings act like palladium and some don't
blurb: A dataset of 550+ nickel Suzuki couplings sorted by ligand heteroatom identity, hybridization, bite angle, and buried volume to find what actually splits base-metal radical pathways from noble-metal-style mechanisms. Turns out it's ligand hardness, not the features people usually screen for. Useful if you're picking ligands for alkyl electrophiles instead of guessing and hoping.

original_title: Photocascade Catalysis: Access to Arene Endoperoxides as Singlet Oxygen Batteries Through Oxyfluoroalkylation and Photooxygenation
title: Storing singlet oxygen in a bottle, one photocascade at a time
blurb: A one-pot cascade bolts photoredox oxyfluoroalkylation onto photooxygenation to build arene endoperoxides, essentially batteries that release singlet oxygen on demand. Most EnT-SET cascades to date just isomerize alkenes, so stacking peroxide synthesis onto that framework is the actual move here.

original_title: Redox-Active Leaving Group Enables the Deoxygenative Arylation of Unactivated Aliphatic Alcohols by Thermal, Homogeneous Iron(I)-Catalyzed Cross-Coupling
title: Turning an alcohol into an aryl group without ever making a halide
blurb: A 2-isoquinolinyl ether leaving group lets an iron(I) metalloradical rip the C(sp3)-O bond homolytically, confirmed by spin trapping, to generate an alkyl radical straight off an unactivated aliphatic alcohol. Radical clock experiments back the mechanism, and the iron(II) catalyst then runs the Kumada coupling to arylate it, skipping the usual tosylate or halide detour.

original_title: Zymeworks Presents New Phase 1 Data for Folate Receptor Alpha-Targeting Antibody-Drug Conjugate ZW191 at ESMO Congress 2026 - mykxlg.com
title: Zymeworks puts fresh phase 1 numbers on its FRα ADC
blurb: New phase 1 data on ZW191, Zymeworks' folate receptor alpha-targeting ADC, out at ESMO. No actual numbers to repeat here, so hold off on getting excited until the readout itself surfaces.

original_title: Merging Mechanochemistry With Double Denitrogenation: Pd‐Catalyzed Cross‐Coupling of Arylhydrazides and Arenediazonium Salts
title: Ball-milling your way to biaryls, no organometallic nucleophile required
blurb: First ball-milled, double denitrogenative Pd coupling of arylhydrazides with arenediazonium salts, kicking out two equivalents of N2 instead of stoichiometric metal waste to make unsymmetrical biaryls. Mechanochemistry doing double duty here, both the energy source and the sustainability pitch.

original_title: Copper‐Catalyzed Substrate‐Controlled Assembly of 1,3,5‐Triazines From Aldehydes and Ammonium Acetate
title: Triazines straight from aldehydes, no prefunctionalized nitrogen needed
blurb: Copper catalysis strings aldehydes and plain ammonium acetate into 2,4,6-trisubstituted 1,3,5-triazines, symmetrical or not, across aromatic, heteroaryl, fused-ring, and even metallocene aldehydes. Mechanistic work points to radical intermediates and nitriles forming en route, a tidier origin story than most triazine routes bother with.

original_title: Protease-Catalyzed Aldol Condensation To Access Axially and Centrally Chiral Biaryls
title: Letting a protease build your atropisomers for you
blurb: An enzymatic aldol desymmetrization sets a carbon stereocenter and a biaryl axis in the same step, hitting up to >99:1 er and >19:1 dr. It also runs at high substrate loading under mild conditions, which is the detail that'll actually get people to try it instead of just citing it.

original_title: Sulfation enabled dynamic activation and single-atom extraction against SO2 poisoning
title: Letting the catalyst poison itself into working better
blurb: Conventional wisdom says sulfate from SO2 kills oxidation catalysts, but here sulfation of a Pt1/MnTiO2 single-atom catalyst forms a Pt1-SO4 motif that turns out to be the active site, not the dead end. Benzene oxidation holds up for 300 hours straight in 100 ppm SO2 at 240°C, the number that matters if you've ever watched an industrial VOC catalyst get sulfur-poisoned.

original_title: Visible light-induced cyanomethylation/aminomethylation of acrylamides: divergent synthesis of cyanomethyl/aminomethyl-substituted N -heterocycles and acyclic amides
title: One photoreaction, four heterocycle flavors depending how you tune the substrate
blurb: Photocatalytic cyanomethylation or aminomethylation of acrylamides branches into indolinones, isoquinolinediones, pyrrolidinones, or plain acyclic amides just by adjusting substrate structure. The mechanistic work actually explains why each path wins where it does, rather than just reporting the split and moving on.

original_title: Photocatalytic Cascade Cyclization of Unactivated Alkenes With N ‐Aminopyridinium Salts Toward Tetrahydropyridazine and Dihydropyrazole Derivatives
title: Blue LED cascade builds two bonds' worth of ring in one go
blurb: N-aminopyridinium salts plus unactivated alkenes under a 10 W blue LED cascade straight into tetrahydropyridazines or dihydropyrazoles, forming both new bonds in a single step across 41 examples. Yields run 17-82%, so the scope is real but uneven, and they've already shown the products take further derivatization.

original_title: Photoinduced Phosphinylation/Cyclization of 1,5‐Enenitriles for the Synthesis of Phosphinylated Pyrrolidine‐2,4‐diones
title: Blue light builds phosphinylated pyrrolidinediones, no metal needed
blurb: A metal-free radical cascade under blue light stitches diarylphosphine oxides onto N-tethered enenitriles to close phosphinylated pyrrolidine-2,4-diones, with broad functional group tolerance and gram-scale runs. Radical-trapping experiments pin it on a phosphorus-centered radical, and LCMS turned up two unidentified minor phosphorus byproducts nobody's bothered to characterize yet.

original_title: A General Red‐Light Photocatalytic Platform for the Synthesis of Perfluoroalkyl Tellanes
title: Red light makes perfluoroalkyl tellurides instead of UV
blurb: A general route to perfluoroalkyl tellanes (R_F-Te-R) from ditellanes and perfluoroalkyl iodides, run under red-light irradiation with cheap zinc phthalocyanine as the photocatalyst generating the perfluoroalkyl radicals. Mild and operationally simple is the pitch; whether this underdeveloped compound class actually gets used is on the field, not the method.

original_title: Active Metal Template Synthesis of Rotaxanes From BINOL‐Phosphate Macrocycles
title: Building chiral rotaxanes with a BINOL-phosphate macrocycle as the template
blurb: Cu(I)-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition templated on BINOL-phosphate macrocycles threads the axle and locks in the mechanical bond, with thread length and ring size both tuned and hydroxyl- or amino-bearing alkynes tolerated. Good yields across a range of chiral [2]rotaxanes, so the method reads as generally applicable rather than a one-off trick.

original_title: Nickel‐Catalyzed Regio‐ and Stereoselective Three‐Component Difunctionalization of Alkynes
title: Where nickel-catalyzed alkyne difunctionalization stands right now
blurb: A review rounding up three-component alkyne difunctionalizations under nickel, split into straight single-nickel catalysis versus photoredox/nickel dual catalysis, with the single-Ni side leaning on ligand design for regio- and stereocontrol. A map of the field, not a new result.

original_title: Exploiting Carboxylate Effects to Enhance Cp*Co III -Catalyzed C–H Functionalization
title: The right carboxylate additive matters more than anyone credited in Cp*Co C–H activation
blurb: Carboxylates get tossed into Cp*Co(III) C–H functionalization as an afterthought, but high-throughput screening shows the choice actually controls catalyst speciation and efficiency, especially with weakly coordinating directing groups. Mesitoic acid beat the conventional carboxylates for hydrogen isotope exchange, the kind of fix that's boring until you're the one running the reaction.

original_title: An Alkali Amide Approach to Triphosphabenzenes
title: LiNMe2 catalyzes its way to a Dewar triphosphabenzene
blurb: Simple commercial organolithium reagents cyclotrimerize a phosphaalkyne into 2,4,6-tris(triphenylmethyl)-Dewar-1,3,5-triphosphabenzene, with LiNMe2 doing the catalysis. The solvent decides the mechanism: noncoordinating solvents keep it catalytic, but THF traps a cyclic anion intermediate mid-reaction instead of letting LiNMe2 leave.

original_title: Sulfotransferase Catalyzed Resolution and Nucleophilic Substitution of Alcohols to Access N-H-Heterocycles
title: Sulfotransferases double up: resolving alcohols and building N-H heterocycles
blurb: A sulfotransferase catalyzes kinetic resolution of alcohols and then nucleophilic substitution to deliver N-H heterocycles, folding separation and bond formation into a single enzymatic step.

original_title: A Zwitterionic Indylene with Ambiphilic Redox Reactivity
title: An indium(I) center that acts as both electron donor and acceptor
blurb: A zwitterionic indylene propped up by an anionic bis(NHC)borate ligand shows a narrow HOMO-LUMO gap and an arene stabilizing the vacant indium p orbital, giving the In(I) center genuine ambiphilic character. That donor-acceptor duality shows up in real coordination chemistry and redox reactivity, pushing indium further into territory usually reserved for transition metals.

original_title: A Stable Terminal Mercury Hydride and Its Reactivity To Form Mercury–Metal Bonds
title: Finally isolating a mercury hydride that doesn't fall apart
blurb: Organomercury hydrides are usually fleeting intermediates nobody catches, but a bulky fluorenyl-hydrindacene scaffold stabilizes an arylmercury hydride enough to isolate and fully characterize. It goes on to react with metalloradicals and metal hydrides to form unsupported mercury-metal bonds, suggesting these aren't as inherently unstable as assumed.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Translating non-clinical proof-of-concept data into paediatric development decisions: the case of HER2-targeting antibody-drug conjugates
title: Why pediatric cancer trials shouldn't just follow the adult indication
blurb: EU pediatric drug rules are built around the adult indication a drug got approved for, which can miss mechanisms that matter in kids' cancers even when the approved use doesn't apply. Using HER2-targeting antibody-drug conjugates as the worked example, the case is for reviewing mechanism and target relevance case by case instead of defaulting to a waiver, with EU practice apparently already drifting that direction.

original_title: AI-driven discovery and engineering of human-derived protein scaffolds for mRNA delivery
title: Mining the human proteome for an mRNA delivery vehicle your immune system already recognizes
blurb: Viral and non-viral vectors work but trip immune responses because they're built from non-human parts, so this team screened the entire human proteome with an AI platform called DeepDelivery and flagged 512 candidate proteins. 80% of the top hits actually packaged mRNA into particles and delivered it, a solid hit rate for a first unbiased screen.

original_title: Novel Synthetic Strategies and Mechanistic Insights in the Synthesis of Trifluoromethoxylated Compounds
title: OCF3 groups are great for drug design and miserable to install
blurb: A review of why putting a trifluoromethoxy group on a molecule is such a pain: the anion falls apart on its own, bench-stable reagents are scarce, and that's before regioselectivity even comes up. Worth a read if you're staring down an OCF3 target and want to know which strategies actually hold up.

original_title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Heck‐Type Double Arylation of 1,2‐Dihydropyridines
title: Two aryl groups onto a dihydropyridine, your choice of same or different
blurb: Pd-catalyzed Heck-type double arylation turns dearomatized pyridines into 3,6-diarylated 1,2-dihydropyridines. One route slaps on two identical aryl groups in one shot, the other does it stepwise so you can put different aryls on each position, and both stay site- and regioselective across a decent range of substrates.

original_title: Precise modular engineering of neutral organometallic rectangles from binuclear palladacycles via hierarchical assembly strategy
title: Getting neutral Pd-carbon cages to self-correct despite being kinetically stubborn
blurb: Metal-carbon bonds are usually too locked-in for the error-correcting self-assembly that makes supramolecular cages work, so this group used binuclear palladacycles as preorganized building blocks and staged the assembly in steps instead of all at once. Getting robust Pd-C architectures to behave like a reversible system is the harder half of this paper, not just stacking the pieces.

original_title: Tandem Allene Formation/Intramolecular Cyclization of Phosphorus‐Substituted Propargylic Alcohols and Substituted Phenols to Access C4‐Phosphorylated 2 H ‐Chromenes
title: Propargylic alcohols to C4-phosphorylated chromenes in one pot, no glovebox needed
blurb: Phosphorus-substituted propargylic alcohols react with phenols under In(ClO4)3 or Hg(ClO4)2 catalysis, running an SN1' substitution into a 6-endo-trig cyclization through an allene intermediate, landing on C4-phosphorylated 2H-chromenes. Mild enough to run in air at 40-60°C, which is the actual selling point for a phosphorylation route.

original_title: Enzymatic crosslinking and hydrolysis of insect proteins: Implications for IgE-mediated cross-reactivity and ACE-inhibitory activity.
title: Processing insect protein changes both its allergy risk and its blood pressure effects
blurb: Enzymatically crosslinking and hydrolyzing insect proteins shifts two things at once: IgE cross-reactivity, whether your immune system mistakes it for a known allergen, and ACE-inhibitory activity, the blood-pressure-lowering effect prized in food protein hydrolysates. Relevant if insect protein is heading into food products and allergenicity is the thing nobody wants to discover after the fact.

original_title: Photocatalytic Direct Desulfurization of Glycosyl Thiols via Glycosyl Radicals for the Synthesis of gem -Difluoroalkene C -Alkyl Glycosides
title: Turning bench-stable glycosyl thiols into gem-difluoroalkene glycosides by just knocking the sulfur off
blurb: Photocatalysis strips the sulfur from stable glycosyl thiols to generate glycosyl radicals, which then run a radical-polar crossover into gem-difluoroalkene C-alkyl glycosides with high stereoselectivity. It tolerates a wide range of functional groups, scales to grams, and the mechanism turns up a transient pyridyl thioglycoside intermediate along the way.

original_title: From Photo-crosslinking to Covalent: A Cascade DNA-Encoded Library Strategy for Pin1 Inhibitor Discovery
title: Finding new Pin1 covalent warheads without starting from a known scaffold
blurb: Covalent Pin1 inhibitors have mostly been built off known affinity scaffolds or straight covalent screening, so this cascade DNA-encoded library strategy pairs photo-crosslinking selection with a switch to covalent targeting to design new covalent binders from scratch. Pin1's been a drug target for years; a de novo route into its covalent chemical space is the actual news here.

original_title: Quantitative Multiplexed Rapid Immunoprecipitation and Mass Spectrometry of Endogenous Proteins (qPLEX‐RIME) in Cell Lines
title: RIME gets multiplexed and quantitative, no affinity tags required
blurb: qPLEX-RIME pulls down endogenous protein complexes, chromatin factors and transcription factors especially, straight off the native protein with no genetically encoded tag needed. The method fixes twice, first DSG then formaldehyde, before IP and mass spec, which locks in weak or transient complex members a single fixation step would lose.

original_title: Carbon‐Supported Catalytic Systems Assembled by π–π Interactions
title: Sticking catalysts to carbon with nothing but pi-stacking
blurb: Pyrene-tagged catalysts cling to carbon supports through pi-pi interactions alone, no covalent anchor needed, and still deliver the recovery and recycling benefits of immobilization plus less metal contamination in the product. The appeal is that it's reversible, so swapping or regenerating the catalyst doesn't mean rebuilding the whole support.

original_title: Letts synthesis of benzonitrile
title: Letts synthesis of benzonitrile
blurb: The Letts synthesis is an old, accessible, and quite unusual method of preparing nitriles from carboxylic acids. The general reaction consists in heating a mixture of sources of carboxylate and thiocyanate. I dry-distilled zinc benzoate and lead rhodanide over an alcohol burner as per the procedure outlined in Houben's Die Methoden der Organischen Chemie , which claims to give a 80% yield. I couldn't get around to purifying the nitrile and didn't record the yield, but it was seemingly good.
